questions.question: Describe dribbling technique and training drills in Handball. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe dribbling technique and training drills in Handball.
  • Dribbling in handball means bouncing the ball continuously while moving.
  • Technique:
  • Keep knees slightly bent
  • Use fingertips, not palm
  • Push the ball downward with control
  • Keep head up to observe surroundings
  • Use either hand while moving
  • Types of Dribble
  • High Dribble: Used for fast breaks or moving quickly down the court when defenders are not nearby.
  • The ball is bounced roughly at waist level.
  • Low Dribble: A defensive, protective dribble used when closely guarded, where the ball is bounced
  • below the knee level to minimize turnover risk.

questions.question: Explain the rule regarding scoring a goal in hockey. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the rule regarding scoring a goal in Hockey
  • A goal is scored in hockey when the ball is legally played by an attacking player and completely
  • crosses the goal line between the goalposts and under the crossbar.
  • Important rules:
  • The ball must be hit from inside the striking circle
  • No foul should occur before scoring
  • If the ball is played from outside the circle, the goal is not valid
  • Umpire confirms whether the goal is legal
  • Each valid goal gives one point to the team.

questions.question: Fault rules are the backbone of badminton.” Justify this statement. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• “Fault rules are the backbone of badminton.” Justify this statement.
  • Fault rules are important because they maintain discipline, fairness, and proper conduct in badminton.
  • Examples of faults:
  • Shuttle lands outside boundary lines
  • Shuttle passes under or through the net
  • Player touches the net
  • Player hits the shuttle twice
  • Wrong service or service from incorrect side
  • Server’s feet not in correct position
  • These rules prevent unfair advantage and ensure smooth gameplay. Without fault rules, the game
  • would become disorganized and unfair.
